meta.title_index: Folito: EPUB Reader for Apple Watch
meta.description_index: Folito is an EPUB reader for Apple Watch: import your own books on iPhone and read them offline on your wrist. No account needed; sync is optional.
meta.description_privacy: How Folito, the EPUB reader for Apple Watch, handles your data: no developer accounts, no ads, no analytics. Optional sync uses a service you choose.
meta.description_support: Help for Folito, the EPUB reader for Apple Watch: getting started, importing books, optional sync with KOReader Sync or Readest, dictionaries, FAQ.
picker.label: Language
footer.legal: Folito is an independent app. KOReader and Readest are names of third-party projects, used only to describe compatibility; Folito is not affiliated with or endorsed by them. Apple, Apple Watch and iPhone are trademarks of Apple Inc.
index.tagline: An EPUB reader for Apple Watch. Bring your own books; no account needed.
index.watch_label: Screenshot of Folito on Apple Watch: the reader at the opening of Pride and Prejudice
index.what_lede: A full reading app, designed for the smallest screen you own.
index.f1_text: Import your own .epub books on the iPhone (Files, the share sheet or the import button). They are sent to your watch, where you read them offline. Covers, series and descriptions come from the EPUB itself.
index.f2_text: Choose the font, text size, line, paragraph and letter spacing, margins, heading size and a reading theme, on the watch or the iPhone. The book text can also follow your watch's own text size.
index.f3_text: Offline word lookup on the watch with free dictionaries built from Wiktionary by reader.dict (CC BY-SA 4.0): English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese and Chinese, downloaded on the iPhone. If the book's language has no dictionary on the watch, Folito says which one is missing and where to get it.
index.f4_text: Optional: sync your reading progress with a KOReader Sync server or with Readest Cloud, and continue in KOReader or the Readest apps. Sync moves forward only: the watch offers to jump only when another device is further ahead. It stays off until you sign in with your own account; the developer runs no server.
index.f5_text: VoiceOver, Dynamic Type, Bold Text, Increase Contrast and Dark Mode on the iPhone and the watch. Reading themes meet WCAG contrast ratios.
index.f6_text: No accounts with the developer, no ads, no analytics, no tracking. The developer runs no server and receives no data.
index.f7_text: The reader estimates the time left in the chapter and the book from your own reading speed. A watch-face complication or the Smart Stack shows your progress and takes you back to your page.
index.f8_text: Signed in to Readest, the iPhone Library also lists the books in your Readest library. Browse them, download one to your iPhone and watch, or upload your own books to Readest.
index.f9_text: Only if you ask: the iPhone can fill in a missing cover or description from Open Library, for one book or for every new import. Off by default; nothing is looked up otherwise.

index.books_sources: Folito reads EPUB files without DRM. You can get them from public-domain libraries such as Project Gutenberg and Standard Ebooks, from stores and publishers that sell DRM-free EPUBs, or use the files you already have.
index.books_drm: Books bought with DRM from Kindle, Apple Books or Kobo will not open.
index.books_ways: To add a book, open the file from the Files app or the share sheet on your iPhone and choose Folito, or tap Import EPUB in the Library. If you sign in to Readest, the Library also lists the books in your Readest library, ready to download. Just want to try it? The app includes a short sample book in your language.
index.req_price: Free, with every feature included: no in-app purchases, ads, accounts or analytics.
index.req_ios: An iPhone with iOS 17 or later.
index.req_watch: An Apple Watch with watchOS 10 or later: Apple Watch Series 4 or later, including Apple Watch SE and Apple Watch Ultra.
index.req_note: Books are imported on the iPhone and sent to the paired watch; no account is needed.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.updated: Last updated: 10 November 2026. Applies to the Folito apps for iPhone and Apple Watch.
privacy.summary: In short: Folito works without any account. It has no analytics, no advertising and no tracking, and the developer runs no server and receives no data. The app only contacts a sync server if you choose to set one up, and the dictionary download site named below when you download a dictionary. If you ask it to, the iPhone also looks up missing book details on Open Library (see below).
privacy.local_1: Your books (EPUB files you import or download from Readest) are processed and stored in the app's storage on your iPhone, which also keeps the original EPUB file, and sent to your Apple Watch over Apple's WatchConnectivity, directly between your paired devices. The app uploads a book only to your own Readest account, and only when you ask it to (see below).
privacy.local_2: Your reading positions, typography settings, a random device identifier (see below) and, if sync is on, progress waiting to be synced are stored in the app's settings on the device. Your typography settings are also sent to your paired watch. To estimate the time left in a book, the watch also learns your reading speed and keeps it there; the estimate is shown on your paired iPhone too.
privacy.local_3: Dictionaries you download are stored on your iPhone and your Apple Watch. Words are looked up on the watch itself, so what you look up never leaves the device. You can delete dictionaries in the iPhone app (Settings › Dictionaries).
privacy.local_4: Your sync login, only if you turn sync on (server address, username, password), is stored in the Keychain on your iPhone. Because the watch syncs on its own, the server address, the username and a hash (MD5) of the password, never the password itself, are also sent to your paired watch over WatchConnectivity and stored in the watch's own Keychain. Until the watch has received them, the system keeps that message in its transfer queue on your iPhone, outside the Keychain; the same applies to the Readest session described below. Your login is never sent to the developer, and over the internet it goes only to the sync server you entered (see the next section).
privacy.local_readest: Your Readest sessions, only if you choose Readest for sync: your Readest email and two session tokens (never your Readest password) are stored in the Keychain on your iPhone: one for the iPhone's Library, which stays on the iPhone, and one for sync, which is sent to your paired watch and stored in its own Keychain.
privacy.local_5: The app does not use iCloud. Deleting the app removes this data from that device.
privacy.sync_title: Reading-progress sync (optional, your KOReader Sync server)
privacy.sync_intro: Sync is off unless you turn it on. You do not need any account to import and read books. If you enter a KOReader Sync server, username and password and turn sync on, the app sends requests only to that server. (The server field suggests https://sync.koreader.rocks, the public KOReader server; nothing is sent to it until you save a username and password, and you can change it to your own server.) The app does not create accounts; you use an account you already have on that server. Requests can include:
privacy.sync_1: your username and an MD5 hash of your password (this is how the KOReader Sync protocol authenticates; your password itself is not sent to the server);
privacy.sync_2: a book identifier, which is a hash computed from the content of the EPUB file (not the file, its title or its text);
privacy.sync_3: your reading position in that book (a position reference and a percentage);
privacy.sync_4: the device name "Folito" and a random identifier generated by the app on first launch (it is not derived from your device's hardware and is not an advertising identifier).
privacy.sync_outro: The app does not send a timestamp to a KOReader Sync server; the server records its own. As with any internet request, the server sees your IP address. That server is run by whoever operates it (you, or a service you chose), not by the developer; its own privacy policy and retention rules apply, and the app cannot delete data stored there (ask the server operator). If you use http:// (allowed only for local-network addresses; iOS asks for local network permission the first time) the traffic is not encrypted. If you do not turn sync on, no sync requests are made.
privacy.readest_title: Reading-progress sync with Readest (optional, your Readest account)
privacy.readest_intro: Instead of a KOReader Sync server you can choose Readest in Settings › Progress Sync and sign in with a Readest account you already have; only one sync service is active at a time. Readest is a third-party service, not run by the developer, and Folito is not affiliated with it. When you sign in, your email and password are sent once over HTTPS to Readest's sign-in service (operated for Readest by Supabase); Folito does not store your password, only the session it receives. While sync is on, the app sends to Readest (web.readest.com):
privacy.readest_1: the session token that identifies your Readest account (renewed about once an hour by the watch);
privacy.readest_2: two book identifiers: a hash computed from the content of the EPUB file and a hash of the book's title, authors and identifier (not the file, its title or its text in readable form);
privacy.readest_3: your reading position in that book (a position reference, the paragraph number and count) and when you reached it.
privacy.readest_outro: Unlike a KOReader Sync server, Readest does receive the time you reached each position: its service uses it to keep the most recent one. No device identifier is sent to Readest. Readest stores your reading position in your Readest account, where the Readest apps and the Readest plugin for KOReader read it; Readest's privacy policy and terms apply, and data stored there is managed in Readest (the app cannot delete it). Sign Out in Settings › Progress Sync removes the session from your iPhone and Apple Watch and asks Readest to end it. If you do not choose Readest, nothing is sent to Readest.
privacy.dict_text: Looking up a word sends nothing anywhere: the dictionaries are on your watch. Only when you tap Download or Update in Settings › Dictionaries does the iPhone download a dictionary file over HTTPS from www.reader-dict.com (reader.dict, which compiles the files from Wiktionary). The request contains only the file's address, which shows the language you chose, and a User-Agent naming the app; the site sees your IP address and handles it under its own policy. While that screen is open, the app also asks the site (same information, no file transferred) whether an installed dictionary has changed. The iPhone then converts the file and sends it to your watch over the Apple Watch connection. No word, book title, text or reading position is ever sent.
privacy.online_title: Book details from Open Library (optional, iPhone only)
privacy.online_text: Covers and details are read from the EPUB file itself, and nothing is looked up online unless you ask. You can ask in two ways: Find Details Online in a book's details (once, for that book), or Settings › Book Details, where Find Missing Details Online (off by default) looks up books you import from then on that have no cover or description, and Look Up Missing Details Now does the same for the books you already have. The iPhone then asks Open Library (openlibrary.org and covers.openlibrary.org, run by the non-profit Internet Archive; cover images may be served from archive.org) over HTTPS. The request contains only the book's ISBN, or, without one, its title and first author, plus a User-Agent naming the app. Nothing about you, your account, your reading or the rest of your library is sent, and the developer receives nothing. Open Library sees your IP address and handles it under the Internet Archive's privacy policy. Details you accept are stored only on your iPhone, next to the book, and marked "From Open Library"; they fill only what the EPUB lacks and never change the EPUB file. Remove Online Details in the book's details deletes them again.
privacy.online_readest: If you upload a book to your Readest account and it has a cover you accepted from Open Library (because the EPUB has none), that cover is uploaded as the book's cover image in your Readest storage, like a cover taken from the EPUB.
privacy.not_1: No analytics, crash-reporting, advertising or other third-party SDKs, and no tracking across apps or websites.
privacy.not_2: No accounts with the developer; the developer receives no data from the app.
privacy.not_3: No sale or sharing of data.
privacy.children_text: The app is not directed at children and the developer collects no personal information from anyone.
privacy.rights_text: Sync is optional. To stop syncing, open Settings › Progress Sync on the iPhone and tap Turn Off Sync and Remove Login: the login is removed from your iPhone and your Apple Watch, and progress waiting to sync is discarded (your books and reading positions are kept). You can also remove the login on the watch alone (Settings › Remove Credentials), delete dictionaries, or delete the app at any time. For data held by a sync server or the dictionary download site, contact that service. For questions about this policy, write to xlahuerta@protonmail.com.
privacy.rights_readest: If you use Readest, tap Sign Out in Settings › Progress Sync to remove the session from both devices; your Readest account and the progress stored in it are managed in Readest.
privacy.changes_text: If the app's behaviour changes, this page will be updated and the date above changed.
support.title: Support
support.contact: Questions, bug reports or feature requests: xlahuerta@protonmail.com. Please include your iOS and watchOS versions and, if the problem is syncing, which server software you use. Never send your password.
support.start_1: Install Folito on your iPhone; the watch app installs through the Watch app on the iPhone (or automatically). Open the iPhone app once so the watch can be set up.
support.start_2: Import an .epub you own or a free public-domain one: tap Import EPUB (+) in the Library, or open the file from the Files app or the share sheet and choose Folito. The book is sent to your watch. To try it first, tap Add a Sample Book in the welcome tour or the empty Library: it adds a short public-domain book in your language.
support.start_3: Open Folito on the watch and choose the book. Your place is saved on the watch, and reading works offline.
support.sync_title: Optional: sync with a KOReader Sync server
support.sync_1: Sync is off by default and only needed to continue the same book in KOReader or another app that speaks the KOReader Sync protocol. On the iPhone open Settings › Progress Sync, set Sync Service to KOReader Sync, enter the server URL and the username and password of an account you already have on that server (create it on the server itself, for example in KOReader under Tools › Progress sync › Register; Folito does not create accounts), tap Save and Turn On Sync, then Test Connection. The login is sent to your watch so it can sync on its own.
support.sync_2: To stop syncing, tap Turn Off Sync and Remove Login: the login is removed from the iPhone and the watch; your books and reading positions are kept.
support.readest_1: Use this to continue the same book in the Readest apps, or in KOReader with the Readest plugin. On the iPhone open Settings › Progress Sync, set Sync Service to Readest, enter the email and password of the Readest account you already have and tap Sign In and Turn On Sync. The password is not stored; the watch receives the session and syncs on its own.
support.readest_2: Use the same EPUB file on every device: positions are matched by file. Positions are saved per paragraph, so you continue at the start of the paragraph you were reading. To stop, tap Sign Out.
support.dict_1: On the iPhone open Settings › Dictionaries and tap Download next to a language. The dictionary is sent to your watch, where word lookup then works offline. Tap Update when a newer version is available.
support.dict_2: The dictionaries are compiled from Wiktionary by reader.dict; Wiktionary content is available under CC BY-SA 4.0. The credits are also in Settings › Acknowledgements.
support.dict_3: If you look up a word in a book whose language has no dictionary on the watch, Folito tells you which dictionary is missing and where to download it. On the iPhone, a book's details also offer the dictionary for its language when one is available.
support.reading_1: In Folito's settings on the watch or the iPhone, Typography sets the font, text size, line, paragraph and letter spacing, margins, heading size and the reading theme. With Match System Text Size on, the book text follows the Text Size setting of your Apple Watch.
support.reading_2: To see your progress at a glance, add the Folito complication to a watch face or find Folito in the Smart Stack; tap it to go back to your page. The reader also estimates the time left in the chapter and the book from your own reading speed.
support.a1: No. Importing and reading need no account of any kind. Sync is optional and uses a service you choose (a KOReader Sync server or your Readest account); the developer runs no server.
support.a2: Any KOReader Sync (kosync) compatible server, including the public KOReader server and self-hosted ones. The app does not provide a server.
support.q3: Progress does not match in KOReader or Readest.
support.a3: It must be the same, unmodified EPUB file on every device. In Readest set the document matching method to File Content; in KOReader use Binary.
support.q4: My http:// server does not connect.
support.a4: iOS blocks plain http to internet hosts. Use https, or a local-network address (iOS asks for local network permission the first time).
support.q5: Word lookup says there is no dictionary or no definition.
support.a5: Download a dictionary for the book's language in the iPhone app (Settings › Dictionaries). It is sent to the watch and then works offline. If a word is missing, Folito tries simple base forms and your other installed dictionaries. Definitions are in the dictionary's own language (Spanish words are explained in Spanish).
support.a6: The iPhone and watch apps support VoiceOver and larger text sizes (Dynamic Type), follow Dark Mode, Increase Contrast and Bold Text, and use no custom animations. On the watch, reading themes meet WCAG contrast ratios and Typography › Match System Text Size makes the book text follow the watch's text size.
support.q7: Does the app support DRM-protected books?
support.q8: I went back on the watch, but KOReader or Readest still opens further on.
support.a8: Sync moves forward only, like Readest and KOReader. When you open a book, the watch asks whether to continue only if another device is ahead; an earlier synced position is ignored and you stay where you are. To go back to the synced position anyway, open Options in the reader and tap Go to Synced Position. In the other direction, Readest and KOReader keep their furthest position and do not follow a move backwards made on the watch; that is how those apps work and Folito cannot change it.
privacy.readest_library: Your Readest library on the iPhone. While you are signed in to Readest, the Library on your iPhone reads the list of books in your Readest account (titles, authors, file hashes), shows their covers and downloads a book file when you tap it. Book files are uploaded to your Readest account only when you choose Upload to Readest on a book, or turn on Upload Imported Books Automatically (off by default); the file, its title, author and hashes then count against your Readest storage. Delete from Readest removes the file and the book from your Readest account after you confirm it.
support.readest_3: While you are signed in to Readest, the Library also shows the books in your Readest library, with the cloud download symbol. Tap one to download it to your iPhone and Apple Watch; its reading position then syncs exactly, because it is the same file. Touch and hold a book (or swipe it) to Upload to Readest, Remove Download (keeps it in Readest) or Delete. Use the filter button to show all books, only those on this iPhone or only those in Readest.
